messages:
incident-bot: :warning: ALERT — Dedicated GPU pool 'eu-west-2-reserved-3' reporting 100% GPU allocation and autoscaler failing to provision additional instances. Queue depth rising for dedicated tenants.

jin-oncall: paging oncall. Acme Enterprise reporting high latency + 429s on /v1/generate.

alex-runtime: seeing queue growth on the dedicated dispatcher. Metrics: pending requests ~ 480 (baseline 40), avg wait 18s and climbing. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to attach GPUs.

maria-sre: on it. grabbing logs from autoscaler and node-provisioner. @ops-bot can you dump last 30m of autoscaler events?

ops-bot: @maria-sre autoscaler events pulled:
```
2026-09-14T15:02:01Z INFO Attempting scale up by 4
2026-09-14T15:02:04Z ERROR failed to provision: quotaExceeded (Requested: 4 GPUs, Available: 0)
2026-09-14T15:05:12Z INFO Attempting scale up by 2
2026-09-14T15:05:16Z ERROR rate limit from provider: ResourceAllocationDenied
2026-09-14T15:08:47Z WARN noisyNeighborDetector: high GPU memory churn on node pool eu-west-2-burst
```

alex-runtime: quotaExceeded + provider rate limits. Looks like reserved capacity exhausted and cloud provider refusing new nodes. That matches the dedicated pool commit being fully utilized.

beth-cs: Customer impact: Acme Enterprise (reserved) seeing throttled requests and errors. They reported degraded SLAs for last 7m. Ticket #CAD-4523.

jin-oncall: escalation status? Should we activate fallback routing to hosted for non-sensitive tenants? Need svc owners' signoff for enterprise traffic.

beth-cs: Acme is enterprise, cannot route to hosted by default. Can request explicit opt-in for emergency fallback. Trying call now.

alex-runtime: quick mitigations we can do now: 1) evict obvious noisy jobs from dedicated pools (best-effort) 2) enable temporary throttling at ingress with informative 429s to reduce queue backpressure 3) route new requests for non-reserved tenants to other regions/hosted.

maria-sre: starting with (1). Running filter to identify pods with >80% persistent GPU memory and long-running single jobs.

ops-bot: candidate pods flagged:
- gpu-job-928 (team: MLBatch) 98% GPU mem, runtime 36h
- render-hf-11 (team: marketing) 91% GPU mem, runtime 20h
- unknown-spotter (team: unknown) 87% GPU mem, runtime 12h

maria-sre: initiating graceful eviction on gpu-job-928 and render-hf-11, will attempt checkpoint and reschedule to non-dedicated queues.

alex-runtime: Eviction command:
```
kubectl -n dedicated delete pod gpu-job-928 --grace-period=60 --wait=false
kubectl -n dedicated annotate pod render-hf-11 "redwood/evicted-for-incident=1789504321"
```

deploy-bot: Eviction jobs submitted. Checkpoint started for gpu-job-928 (job-id 0x7a3f).

maria-sre: Monitoring queue after evictions. Queue depth dropped from 480 -> 320 in 3m. Good signal but still elevated.

jin-oncall: next: apply ingress-level throttles with clear retry-after for non-enterprise tenants. Can we push a rule?

alex-runtime: Pushing temporary rule now to limiter config: reduce burst to 20, per-key rate to 5r/s for non-reserved routes. Command:
```
redwoodctl limiter apply --scope global --selector "!reserved_tenant" --burst 20 --rate 5
```

ops-bot: Limiter update applied in 55s. Observability shows 12% immediate reduction in incoming TPS to dedicated pool.

beth-cs: Acme on the call: they explicitly DON'T want fallback to hosted. Accepting degraded performance, want communications templates. Drafting now.

sylvia-pm: FYI Product asked for immediate status update to enterprise dashboard and support banner. Beth, send copy; I'll coordinate.

maria-sre: autoscaler: we are still seeing provider quota errors. Opening ticket with cloud provider and contacting capacity team to request temporary burst from spare pools.

alex-runtime: Another lever: enable model-variant downgrade for latency-sensitive routes for those tenants that allow it (e.g., smaller quantized variant to reduce GPU time). Can toggle per-tenant.

 beth-cs: Confirmed from Acme: they will allow model-downgrade for a subset of endpoints (risk acceptance recorded). Proceed.

alex-runtime: Applying model-variant policy for tenant acme-enterprise to route non-critical generate-> generate-quant-small. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set --tenant acme-enterprise --route "/v1/generate" --variant generate-quant-small --reason "incident 1789504321"
```

ops-bot: Routing change accepted by control-plane, warming model caches. Cache hit % initially low; expect latency improvement in ~90s.

maria-sre: After evictions + throttles + variant downgrade, queue depth down to 110, avg wait ~4s. Errors reduced from 12%->2.1%.

jin-oncall: Good. What about noisy neighbor detection long-term? We saw high GPU memory churn on eu-west-2-burst nodes earlier. Need postmortem actions: stricter isolation, preemptible eviction for non-reserved, and better admission controls.

alex-runtime: Agree. Also need to revisit dedicated pool sizing and commit reports — commit utilization at 100% for a while. Recommend capacity uplift or reservation rebalance.

beth-cs: Acme acknowledged immediate mitigation. They want a postmortem and proposed SLA credit review. I've opened PSR for legal/compliance.

sylvia-pm: I'll schedule a cross-functional post-incident review tomorrow 09:00 UTC with SRE, runtime, sales for impacted customers, and capacity planning.

jin-oncall: Wrapping up: 1) Evictions succeeded 2) Throttle applied 3) Model downgrade applied 4) Cloud provider ticket open (CP-9872) 5) Customer notified. Keep this thread updated until cloud provider confirms additional capacity.

deploy-bot: Deploys/changes logged: limiter update, routing policy, pod evictions. Change-ids: CH-5561, CH-5562, CH-5563.

maria-sre: Cloud provider update: responding, offering 2 GPUs from spot pool with 10m lead. Not enough to fully restore but helps. Continuing to push for spare reserved reallocations.

jin-oncall: Thanks all. Handing incident to maria-sre for ongoing mitigation and to beth-cs for customer comms. Oncall handoff: @maria-sre you're primary, @alex-runtime secondary. If anything regresses, page me immediately. :white_check_mark:

maria-sre: Acknowledged. Monitoring for 1 hour and will update status.

beth-cs: I'll send the customer status update now. Template: "We are mitigating a dedicated capacity issue affecting your reserved pool; temporary throttling and model variance changes have been applied to reduce impact. Our SRE team is actively working with our cloud provider.."

incident-bot: Incident thread flagged for postmortem (label: dedicated-capacity-exhaustion, priority: P1).

jin-oncall: Closing active paging for now. Keep thread open for any follow-ups.
